question: What is the main goal of primary health care in our communities?
explanation: Spot on! Primary health care is all about stopping sickness before it starts and keeping people well, rather than waiting for them to need major hospital procedures. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do government health systems often partner with non-governmental agencies?

options.A: Communities prefer private doctors over public nurses
options.B: Ministries of health do not care about rural populations
options.C: Hospitals lack enough space to store modern medicines
options.D: Government facilities face funding limits and personnel shortages

explanation: You got it! Because budgets and staff numbers can be tight, government agencies often need extra hands to reach every corner of the country. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the main driving force behind a non-governmental organization (NGO)?
explanation: Exactly! NGOs exist to help people and serve communities out of goodwill, not to make money. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which group is usually formed by local neighbors to tackle specific health needs in their area?
explanation: Spot on! Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) start right at the grassroots level because local people know what their neighborhood needs most. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h2)

question: How do NGOs commonly help out rural health posts?

options.A: Writing national tax laws for health
options.C: Supplying essential drugs and medical equipment

explanation: You're right! NGOs frequently step in to provide the actual medicines and basic tools that rural clinics are missing. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h3)

question: A village faces a sudden cholera outbreak and needs quick action. What is an NGO most likely to do first?

options.A: Set up emergency treatment units and distribute clean water supplies
options.B: Import expensive surgical equipment for heart transplants
options.C: Close all local food markets permanently to stop trade
options.D: Wait for a two-year legislative budget review by the national assembly

explanation: Spot on! NGOs are fantastic at moving fast during emergencies to set up quick treatment spots and safe water. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main job of the government when working in partnership with NGOs?

options.A: Setting national policies and regulatory oversight

explanation: That's correct! The government sets the rules, guidelines, and standards so that all health activities align nationally. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why can it cause trouble if an NGO runs a health project without involving local health authorities?

options.A: The health program may collapse when donor funding ends
options.B: Local nurses will refuse to treat any sick patients
options.C: The government will fine the community health workers
options.D: The clinic will automatically become a profit-making business

explanation: You got it! Without government ties and local teamwork, projects usually fall apart the moment foreign funders leave. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h4)

question: What financial headache do many NGOs face all the time?

options.A: Excessive government funding with no rules
options.B: Funding instability due to shifting donor priorities
options.C: Making too much profit from free clinics
options.D: Paying excessive taxes on humanitarian donations

explanation: Spot on! NGOs often worry about money because donors frequently change which regions or medical issues they choose to fund. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why do health NGOs often experience high staff turnover?

options.A: Clinics close down every few months due to weather
options.B: Staff members are legally required to change jobs yearly
options.C: They often rely on short-term contracts and lower pay
options.D: Government hospitals steal all qualified nurses by force

explanation: That's right! Because funding comes in short bursts, NGOs often can't offer permanent jobs with great pay, so staff look for stable work elsewhere. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is meant by 'capacity building' in community health projects?

options.A: Increasing the salary of foreign NGO directors
options.B: Purchasing more vehicles for administrative travel
options.C: Building larger physical warehouses for medical drugs
options.D: Training local community members to sustain initiatives

explanation: Exactly! Capacity building is about teaching locals the skills they need to keep running their own health programs successfully. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why should NGOs involve community members right from the project planning stage?

options.A: It prevents the government from inspecting the clinic
options.B: It guarantees that the project will cost zero money
options.C: It ensures cultural acceptance and long-term success
options.D: It stops foreign donors from asking questions

explanation: Spot on! When community members help design a project, they feel proud of it and are much more likely to use and protect the service. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is a key role of a community health nurse when working alongside NGOs?

options.A: Manufacturing medical vaccines in hospital laboratories
options.B: Acting as a bridge between visiting volunteers and local patients
options.C: Auditing the international bank accounts of donor agencies
options.D: Writing new federal health laws for parliament

explanation: You're right! Nurses connect outside volunteers with local residents, making sure everyone understands each other and gets the best care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h7)

question: A nurse receives a batch of donated nutrition teaching materials from an NGO. What is the best way to use them?

options.A: Give them all to private doctors in the city center
options.B: Integrate them into daily antenatal health talks and clinic education
options.C: Throw them away because they did not come from the ministry
options.D: Lock them away in a drawer until the NGO supervisor visits

explanation: Brilliant! Donated materials are most helpful when put straight into daily clinic activities like antenatal talks to educate mothers. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h7)
